Belfast actor Kwame Daniels is gearing up to take a bite out of The Big Apple as his North Star production makes it US debut

Belfast actor Kwame Daniels is gearing up to take a bite out of The Big Apple as his North Star production makes it US debut as he opened up on his 'lifetime's work'.

The boundary-pushing production runs in the Irish Arts Center (IAC) in New York City from June 3rd to 21st 2026, thanks to support from Belfast City Council and the British Council.

The immersive live music and spoken word production came from the Belfast 2024 programme by Daniels and is rooted deeply in Black culture and inspired by the historic 1845 Belfast visit of legendary abolitionist Frederick Douglass. It was first staged at the Telegraph Building during Black History Month 2024 as part of the Belfast International Arts Festival.

The team behind the production includes Grammy Award winner Kaidi Tatham, Northern Irish-Ghanaian artist Winnie Ama, rap dynamo Leo Miyagee, Mercury Prize-nominated Hannah Peel, musical directors Jennifer John and Si Francis and award-winning poet Nandi Jola and actor Colin Salmon.

Creative Director Daniels said: "North Star is a lifetime’s work that brings together all that I am passionate about - connection, creating and collaboration."

The team behind the production includes Grammy Award winner Kaidi Tatham

"The energy of this international cast, which blends the raw talent of young voices from both sides of the Atlantic with premier contemporary musicians, honors Douglass’ vision of unity and global solidarity in a way that feels urgent and alive today."

Belfast Deputy Lord Mayor Councillor Paul Doherty paid tribute to North Star and its highlighting of the city's culture and creativity.

Doherty said: “We’re so proud that our investment in North Star through Belfast 2024 has led to this New York debut – it’s the ideal opportunity to showcase our city’s creative brilliance and highlight why Belfast is a UNESCO City of Music."

"We’re also very grateful to our partners the British Council who have helped make this a reality."

Belfast Deputy Lord Mayor Councillor Paul Doherty paid tribute to North Star and its highlighting of the city's culture and creativity.

"It’s the first of what we hope will be a host of very positive outcomes from our five-year Memorandum of Understanding to boost Belfast’s international cultural profile and create new opportunities for artists, cultural organizations and communities to connect globally."

Doherty labeled Daniels' role in the production as a 'master stroke' for the production's role in re-imagining traditional treatment.

Doherty added: “Kwame Daniels has played a master stroke in assembling this incredibly talented team to reimagine traditional theatre and seamlessly fuse hip-hop, jazz, gospel, electronic, and classical music with provocative spoken word poetry and live choral arrangements.

"US audiences can expect a real treat – and I hope that their experience encourages them to visit Belfast in person, perhaps later this summer, as we host the Fleadh Cheoil for the first time this August.”
